title: Magic Squares In Grid
summary: Determine the number of 3 x 3 subgrids within a given row x col grid that form a magic square.
statement: Determine the number of 3 x 3 subgrids within a given row x col grid that form a magic square. A magic square requires each row, column, and both diagonals to sum to the same value, using distinct numbers from 1 to 9. The grid may include numbers up to 15.
constraints: Count 3-by-3 subgrids containing 1..9 exactly once with equal row, column, and diagonal sums.
hints: A valid window needs both the exact digit multiset and eight equal line sums.
Enumerate 3-by-3 origins, collect nine values and all row/column/diagonal sums.
Accept sorted values 1..9 and one distinct sum.
Those checks are precisely the definition; each origin identifies one candidate window.
editorial: Those checks are precisely the definition; each origin identifies one candidate window.

tests.explanation: The left 3-by-3 window is magic; the right one is not.
Equal sums alone are insufficient because values are not 1 through 9.
